You must be at least 13 to create a GrapMail account. Keep your password private and use the account recovery and security settings if you think someone else has accessed your mailbox.
Use your mailbox for lawful communication. Do not send spam, bulk unsolicited messages, phishing, malware, or messages that harass others. Accounts that misuse the service may be suspended.
A message can be queued, sent, or fail. Check Sent and any delivery notice when timing matters. A queued message is still waiting to be sent.
You can sign out on this device or request account deletion from Settings → Data & privacy. Save any mail you need before deleting your account.
GrapMail uses your account details to create and secure your mailbox. The service stores the addresses, messages, and attachments needed to send, receive, and sync your mail.

Google reCAPTCHA helps protect signup from abuse. If you enable new-mail alerts, GrapMail can register a Firebase device token to deliver notifications to your device. You can change notification access in Android Settings.

Remote images are hidden by default in the message reader. Showing them can contact the sender’s image host. The app also keeps a local mailbox cache so recently loaded mail is available more quickly.

GrapMail offers end-to-end encryption for supported messages. Ordinary email and encrypted messages have different privacy properties. You can manage encryption and review your account details in Settings.
In Settings → Data & privacy, you can review your profile and request deletion. For questions about retention, access, or other privacy requests, use the Grapsee contact link below.
This guide explains how GrapMail works. For Grapsee’s current legal information, use the official page below.
